items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: People made the associations with Beiderbecke and Berigan because they were obvious examples of somebody with a huge talent that blew it

ctx.x: Yeah I remember thinking the movie about Buddy Bolden that came out a couple of years ago was so highly fictionalized, and I assume it was because there’s very little information about him. And to make a whole movie about him, it has to be highly fictionalized I guess.

Well that’s the new version of “Young Man With a Horn” I guess, isn’t it? And nobody pretended, at least at the time, nobody pretended that that was history. People made the associations with Beiderbecke and Berigan because they were obvious examples of somebody with a huge talent that blew it, in the sense of the word.

There’s been a few books out focused on white musicians’ contributions to jazz including our friend Randy Sandke. And I’m going to take a stab at this question — do you think black authors and researchers write differently about blues and jazz than white authors and researchers do?
